questions.answer: I speak Bengali as my mother tongue, and English fairly fluently. I picked up English mostly through school and a lot of self-study, and I use it daily at work, so it's become almost [[instinctive]].

questions.q: Is English widely spoken in your country?
questions.answer: It's widely understood in cities, particularly in business, universities and among younger people. In rural areas, though, Bengali is used for almost everything. English is increasingly seen as a [[gateway]] to better jobs and study opportunities.

questions.q: Would you like to learn another language?
questions.answer: I'd love to learn Arabic, mainly so I can understand the Quran more deeply. I've also considered German, since some students I advise are interested in universities there, so it could give me a [[competitive edge]] at work.

questions.q: Do you find learning languages difficult?
questions.answer: It can be, especially as an adult. Grammar and vocabulary take time, but the real challenge is speaking confidently without fear of mistakes. I think consistent practice and [[immersion]] matter far more than natural talent.

questions.q: Do you think children should learn a foreign language at school?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Children pick up languages far more easily than adults, and early exposure builds confidence. In such an [[interconnected]] world, a second language gives them a real advantage later in life.
